answers.reasoning: A same-arc inscribed angle is half its central angle, and equal arcs subtend equal central angles. A 180-degree central angle subtends a diameter. Arc length is proportional to central angle for a fixed circle. Chord length is 2R sin(θ/2), so it is not generally proportional to θ; doubling the central angle does not generally double the chord.
AB is a diameter, so ∠ACB is a right angle. In right triangle ACB, AB=10 is the hypotenuse and AC=8, hence BC=√(10²−8²)=6. For x=∠CAB, tan x=BC/AC=6/8=3/4, choice ②.
